signals.name: Nvidia
signals.label: Sharpest whale divergence of the Q2-2026 cycle, now heading into FQ2 earnings
signals.detail: Tepper added (+53,500 sh to 1,525,000, ~$305M); Dan Loeb (Third Point) exited 100% (sold all 190,000 sh); Soros bought NVDA puts (bearish overlay); Rep. Michael Rulli's Aug 7 late-filing batch disclosed a fresh NVDA sell alongside AAPL, adding a congressional data point on the bearish side. RESOLVED this run: Nvidia reported FQ2 after Wednesday 26 Aug close -- revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), EPS $2.22 (+111% y/y), data-center sales $89B beat, and FQ3 guidance of $108B topped the $104.2B consensus; shares jumped ~14.5% after-hours, and AWS separately announced a 2-million-GPU order using Nvidia's new Vera CPU.
signals.takeaway: Tepper's add and Loeb's exit are now scored: the print was a decisive beat-and-raise, vindicating the bullish side of last quarter's three-way whale split, with the bearish NVDA-puts/short thesis (Soros overlay, Burry's SOXX short) facing its toughest test yet heading into Thursday's Asia open.

signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Rally holds through the weekend into a live Monday sanctions catalyst
signals.detail: Wednesday 26 Aug (price spine, US close): SLV fell -1.17% to $61.59, GLD -1.58% to $421.32, GDX -2.94% to $102.42, SILJ -1.34% to $32.35, SLVP -1.58% to $41.01, NEM -2.62% to $131.60, GOLD(Barrick) -2.90% to $45.49, PAAS -2.91% to $52.63, AG -1.18% to $20.99, HL -1.05% to $20.70 -- a broad miner-led pullback even as gold/silver FUTURES held up (GC=F +0.50% to $4,661.50, SI=F +0.14% to $68.73), a genuine ETF/futures divergence coinciding with the in-line-but-hot Core PCE print (0.2% m/m, 3.3% y/y) that tempered near-term rate-cut odds. Silver still capped its best month in years (~+17-18% in August) even after Wednesday's pullback. Separately, Barrick and Newmont settled their Nevada Gold Mines dispute for $1.95B (26 Aug), clearing a hurdle for Barrick's planned North America gold-business IPO by year-end -- a fundamental positive for the miner sleeve distinct from the metals-price move.
signals.takeaway: Wednesday's pullback in the ETFs/miners against firm gold/silver futures reads as digestion of a hot-but-in-line PCE print rather than a reversal -- Friday's Jackson Hole (new Fed Chair Warsh's debut keynote) is now the next live catalyst that could extend or break the multi-week uptrend.

signals.name: Energy Fuels
signals.label: Bridgewater's new stake rode out Thursday's dip; Monday's China-sanctions rollout is a fresh wildcard
signals.detail: Bridgewater Associates took a new $2.3M/160,899-share position in Q2-2026 (SEC EDGAR), layering onto CEO/director open-market buys ($12.70-13.08, 7-8 Jul) already on record. UUUU fell -6.40% Thu 20 Aug in the broad AI-fear-driven rare-earth risk-off, then rebounded +8.92% Fri 21 Aug to close at $15.14 (MP Materials similarly: -2.89% Thu, +9.10% Fri to $60.05) -- both names round-tripped the sector-wide de-risking within two sessions. Treasury's Monday sanctions rollout explicitly threatens secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and named China (buyer of ~90% of Iran's oil) without confirming direct targeting -- a new China-trade-friction wrinkle that could sympathy-trade the rare-earth basket even though the direct catalyst is unrelated. Tuesday 25 Aug (price spine): UUUU jumped +7.33% to $15.97 and MP +4.79% to $60.17 -- both re-accelerating alongside the broader metals/miner move rather than fading the Monday pause.
signals.takeaway: A rare case of a macro whale and insiders both accumulating the same rare-earth name; Tuesday's fresh double-digit-adjacent moves in both UUUU and MP suggest the sector rally is broadening beyond precious metals into rare earths.
